subject.title: Cron allows invalid Feishu announce jobs without delivery.to, causing runtime delivery failure

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh one of the two open fork PRs that close this issue, or close/ignore those fork attempts and allow a new narrow OpenClaw PR?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the visible linked fix candidates are stale fork PRs with conflicts while same-repository attempts are closed unmerged, so automation should not start a duplicate repair until maintainers choose the landing path.

options.title: Replace with a narrow target-repo PR
options.body: Close or ignore the stale conflicting fork PRs, then land a fresh focused OpenClaw PR with service/gateway validation and regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt one fork PR
options.body: Choose the cleaner fork PR, rebase/refresh it into the target repository, and complete real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Split UX follow-ups
options.body: Keep this issue focused on create-time validation and track cron audit/diagnostic wording separately.

recommendation.title: Replace with a narrow target-repo PR
recommendation.body: Close or ignore the stale conflicting fork PRs, then land a fresh focused OpenClaw PR with service/gateway validation and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest recent ownership signal for the current cron delivery validation helper and gateway/service boundary touched by the fix.
